guard: a managed Jcode seat whose private sessions directory exists but cannot be written is refused before any create_session reaches the harness, renders the fixed sessions_unwritable code with the path and the errno, and never dies as startup failed (unknown) - while an empty writable directory still starts, joins, and lists nothing
why: #1538: real jcode v0.81.5 accepts create_session on a sessions/ directory it cannot write
and dies only later, while persisting the session during the first turn, so the seat rendered
as `startup failed (unknown)` - a death outside every guard the connector owns. The connector
now answers the question the harness will actually face (can a file be created inside), not
the question a readdir can answer: a readable-but-unwritable directory is the same defect as an
unreadable one, and a missing directory is a first launch that must stay untouched.
M1 is the shipped defect: the refusal removed entirely, so the harness is asked, accepts, and
the seat dies on the first turn - the cell that must go red first names the create_session
that reached the harness. M2 narrows the check to directories the connector can also read,
recreating the exact gap this lane closed (readdir succeeds, the create probe refuses, nothing
stops the launch). M3 makes the render lie by falling back to the scrubbed unknown diagnostic.
M4 and M5 attack the accept control from both sides: refusing a first launch with no directory
yet, and refusing the legitimately empty writable directory the panic-recovery path exists to
serve. M6 is the round-2 reviewer's finding reverted to shape: a directory permission test
(access W_OK) passes a mode-0200 directory because the write bit is set, while every create
inside it fails EACCES - search permission is separate from write - so only the create probe
catches it. M7 removes the probe's own cleanup, so a directory that accepts the write keeps a
stray file and the no-leftovers cell goes red.
No completionMarker: this suite is fail-fast at its first red cell and prints no line common
to both outcomes, so a marker would discard exactly the kills it exists to count.
